newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says 1996 GNP growth within target.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says 1996 GNP growth within target.

text.p: The Philippines on Monday reported gross national product (GNP) growth of 6.8 percent in 1996, which it said was within forecast ranges.
Socio-Economic Planning Secretary Cielito Habito told reporters that gross domestic product growth in 1996 was however below target at 5.5 percent.
The country had forecast 1996 GNP growth at between 6.5-7.5 percent and GDP growth at between 6.0-6.8 percent.
Habito said a slowdown in garment production and in rubber product output was the main reason for the below-forecast growth in GDP.
He said garment exports were outpriced by cheaper labour markets in China, India and Vietnam.
Habito also said that 1995 GNP growth had been revised down to 5.0 percent from the earlier announced 5.5 percent because of some double-counting of income from overseas.
He predicted GNP growth of 6.0-6.5 percent year-on-year in the first quarter of 1997 and a full-year target range of 7.0-8.0 percent.
